claude_only.name: Which system of record assigns the authoritative order number, and in what domain is that number unique?
Is a globally unique document identifier carried alongside the human-visible order number, and which governs when the two disagree?
How is the seller's own sales order identifier captured and correlated to the buyer's order number?
In what exact form must a despatch advice or invoice quote this order so the reference resolves without ambiguity?
How is a revision of the order numbered, and is that number part of the order's identity or an attribute of it?
Which single revision is currently in force at any given instant, and how is that determined?
Are superseded revisions retained in full or reconstructed from a change log, and for how long?
What evidence proves that a stored revision has not been altered since it was issued?
Which controlled code expresses the order type, and from which code list is that value drawn?
Does this order create a firm quantity commitment, a ceiling under which releases are drawn, or a release against an existing ceiling?
If the order is a call-off or release, which framework instrument does it draw against and how is the drawdown recorded?
Does the order type change which lifecycle states, approvals or response rules apply?
Which party roles does this order distinguish, and which of them are mandatory for it to be actionable?
Can one legal entity occupy several roles on the same order, and how is that represented without collapsing the roles?
Where the ordering party differs from the originating requester, which party carries the payment and which carries the requirement?
Under which registered scheme is each party identifier issued, and is the scheme code carried with the value?
Does the issuing registry permit reuse of a retired party identifier, and how does that affect historic orders?
Which electronic address routes the order to the seller, and is it distinct from the party's legal identifier?
Which tax or legal registration identifiers must appear on the order for the transaction to be lawful in the applicable jurisdictions?
Which named role holds authority to commit the buyer for this order's value and category?
What record proves the approval was granted before issuance rather than reconstructed afterwards?
What happens to an order issued without adequate authority, and can it be ratified?
Does issuing this order constitute an offer, or an acceptance of a prior seller offer?
By which modes may the seller accept - express response, signature, or commencement of performance - and which mode was actually used?
Until what moment may the buyer withdraw the order without liability, and how is withdrawal evidenced?
Which law governs the order, and how are conflicting buyer and seller standard terms resolved?
Is the line identifier stable across revisions and responses, or reassigned when lines are added or removed?
May a line carry sub-lines or component items, and does a sub-line inherit the parent's terms?
In which unit of measure is the ordered quantity expressed, and from which code list is that unit drawn?
Is the quantity expressed in consumer units, trade units or packs, and how is the conversion recorded?
Which item identifier governs when seller, buyer and standard trade item identifiers are all present and disagree?
When no coded item identifier exists, what description is sufficient for the line to be unambiguously fulfillable?
Under which classification scheme and version is the item categorised for reporting or regulatory purposes?
Where the item is bespoke, which specification document forms part of the order and how is its version pinned?
Is the unit price stated against a base quantity other than one, and how is the line amount derived from it?
Is the price firm, indicative, or to be determined at delivery, and what rule fixes it if not firm?
In which currency is the order denominated, and is a second currency or conversion rate recorded?
Do the anticipated totals bind the seller, or is the line detail authoritative when totals and lines disagree?
Which event starts the payment period - invoice date, delivery, or acceptance of goods?
Does the order constrain the payment means or instrument the seller may use to collect?
Are early-settlement discounts or late-payment penalties stated, and on what base are they computed?
Which external terms documents are incorporated into this order, and at which version?
What precedence applies between the order face, the incorporated terms and any framework agreement?
How much of the framework's ceiling does this order consume, and who maintains the running balance?
How is each delivery destination identified, and does the identifier denote a legal entity, a function or a physical place?
Is the requested delivery expressed as a single date, a window, or a schedule of dated instalments per line?
When header and line delivery instructions differ, which one governs for that line?
Who may change a requested delivery date without a formal order amendment, and within what limits?
Which trade term applies, under which rules edition, and at exactly which named place?
At what point does risk in the goods pass from seller to buyer under the stated term?
Which costs - carriage, insurance, export and import clearance, duties - fall to each party under the stated term?
Is transfer of title addressed anywhere on the order, given that the trade term does not determine it?
What over- or under-delivery tolerance is permitted per line before the delivery is non-conforming?
May the seller substitute an equivalent item, and who decides equivalence?
Are partial deliveries permitted, and does a partial delivery close the line or leave a residual obligation?
How does each fulfilment event attach back to the specific order line and schedule instalment it discharges?
Which states does an order occupy, and which of them are terminal?
Which event triggers each transition, and is the trigger internal to the buyer or an inbound seller message?
Is the order state stored explicitly or derived from the event history, and which is authoritative on conflict?
What happens when no seller response arrives within the expected window?
Which response codes are recognised at header and line level, and how does each map to an internal order state?
When a response accepts with amendments, does the amended content become binding automatically or require buyer confirmation?
Can several responses relate to one order over time, and which one expresses the current position?
How is acceptance recognised when the seller simply performs instead of sending a response?
Which fields may be amended after issuance, and which require a new order instead?
Does the amendment require the seller's written acceptance to take effect, or does it bind unilaterally?
How is each amendment numbered and linked to the order and revision it changes?
What happens to fulfilment already in progress or already delivered when an amendment takes effect?
Has the seller accepted the order, and does that make this a cancellation of an unaccepted offer or a termination of a contract?
Does the seller claim costs incurred before cancellation, and how is that claim recorded against the order?
What conditions must all lines satisfy before the order may be closed as complete?
May a closed or cancelled order be reopened, and what evidence must the reopening record carry?
From which upstream record did each part of the order's content originate, and was any value manually overridden?
What evidence proves the order was transmitted to, and received by, the intended seller?
Where an order event time and the time it was recorded differ, are both retained and which is used for deadline calculation?
Which actor - human, service account or agent - performed each recorded action on the order?
From which event does the retention clock start for this order, and does a fiscal-year rule apply?
When the order file mixes record categories with different periods, which period governs the whole file?
What suspends disposition, and how is a hold recorded and released?
What proves that an order and its attachments were actually disposed of at the end of retention?
Which fields is each counterparty entitled to see, and which are buyer-internal only?
Under what authority may the order be disclosed to an auditor, forwarder or regulator, and is disclosure logged?
Which roles may change an issued order, and does the seller ever gain write rights over any part of it?
Does the order carry personal data such as named contacts or delivery recipients, and what minimisation applies?
Which profile and customization identifiers does an exchanged projection of this order declare?
Which code lists and versions do the coded fields draw on, and how are version changes handled?
To which syntax-neutral semantic model do the order's terms map, so that two syntaxes can be compared?
Which fields are lost or approximated when the order is projected into a narrower syntax, and is that loss recorded?
Which validation rules are fatal, which are warnings, and who may waive a warning?
On what criteria and within what tolerance is the order matched to receipt and invoice before payment is released?
What happens when a downstream document quotes an order reference that does not resolve, or resolves to a superseded revision?
How is it verified that an order re-imported from an exchanged projection is semantically identical to the source?

grok_only.name: What buyer master-system purchase-order number identifies this commitment for all later responses, changes, cancellations, despatches and invoices?
What seller-assigned sales-order identifier, if any, aliases this purchase order in the seller's system without replacing the buyer number?
What instance UUID distinguishes this document occurrence, and is the payload a copy rather than the original issued order?
How must subsequent invoices or fulfilment messages cite this order so that matching uses the buyer number rather than a seller or transport identifier?
Which order type code applies, and does it mean a buyer-to-seller order (220), an internal enterprise purchase order (105), a blanket order, a call-off, or a consignment order?
In this adoption, is Purchase Order the exchanged buyer-to-seller commitment (UBL Order) or an internal requisition that must not be sent as ORDERS 220?
Which specification identification and business-process profile bind the instance, and which additional elements become mandatory under that profile?
Is the order issued in a bilateral EDI agreement, a Peppol four-corner network, or another collaboration, and which choreography of response documents applies?
When did the buyer issue this order, as an event timestamp distinct from when a gateway or agent later observed or ingested it?
For what period is the order valid as an offer, and what happens if the seller responds after that window?
How is the Peppol date-without-timezone issue date combined with optional issue time into an RFC 3339 event time with seconds and explicit offset for this Dimension?
Who is the buyer legal person or organisation, and which party, endpoint and legal-registration identifiers identify that buyer?
Who is the seller legal person or organisation that is asked to supply, and which identifiers and contacts address that seller?
Which originator, invoicee, consignee, delivery party or freight forwarder, if any, differs from buyer or seller, and where do they sit in the delivery chain?
Which party owns the commercial commitment on the customer side when originator, buyer and invoicee are split across units?
Is this purchase order a sufficiently definite offer under the applicable formation law, including identifiable goods, quantity and price or a method to determine them?
Which formation regime governs (CISG Part II, domestic sale-of-goods law, public-procurement rules, or a trading-partner agreement) and have any writing-requirement reservations been declared?
Who is authorised to issue or amend the order so that the buyer is bound, and how is that authority evidenced?
Must the seller accept expressly, may conduct such as despatch constitute acceptance, and is silent non-response ever treated as acceptance under an established practice?
Which order lines constitute this commitment, and what line identifiers allow invoice and despatch line matching?
For each line, which seller, buyer, manufacturer, catalogue or standard item identifier and item name identify the goods or service?
What quantity and unit of measure are ordered on each line, and is the price base quantity different from the order quantity?
If the item is free text or a service without a catalogue number, what description, attributes or period are required so the seller can identify what to supply?
Which fulfilment obligations does this order contain, and how does each map to an order line rather than to a later despatch?
May the seller substitute items or split deliveries, and did the buyer mark potential acceptable alternatives?
How is each obligation linked to sibling fulfilment execution without treating despatch advice as part of the purchase order?
What document, pricing, tax and requested-invoice currencies apply, and which net unit prices and price base quantities are stated?
Which header and line allowances or charges apply, including charge indicator, reason, base amount, percentage and amount?
What anticipated line-extension, allowance, charge, tax-exclusive, tax-inclusive and payable totals did the buyer manifest, and do they satisfy the Peppol calculation rules?
Is stated TAX only an estimate for matching, and which buyer TAX number is supplied for reverse-charge or similar invoice reporting?
Where should the seller deliver, including consignee location and any final delivery party, and how does that differ from the buyer postal address?
What requested delivery date, period or time window applies at header or line, as event times rather than identifiers?
Which delivery terms or Incoterms-style code and special delivery instructions apply, and who pays freight or documentation charges?
What payment terms and expected means of payment does the buyer request on this order?
What buyer accounting cost string or code must the seller repeat on the invoice for automated booking?
If invoicee differs from buyer, which invoicee party must appear on later invoices, and how does that relate to Peppol Billing buyer reference rules?
What is the current lifecycle state of this order: issued, received, accepted, accepted-with-change, partially accepted, rejected, replaced, or cancelled?
When and how did the seller respond, including response code, reasons for rejection, and whether the response replaces the entire order or only some lines?
Has a contract been concluded by effective acceptance, and at what event time did that acceptance reach the buyer?
If multiple or partial responses exist, which lines remain open, which are accepted, and which require a new buyer order?
What buyer change is in force, does it replace the entire previous order state, and has the seller accepted that change?
Has the buyer issued a cancellation, at what event time, and do contract terms still require fulfilment because manufacture or delivery has begun?
Who has authority to change or cancel, and which trading-partner or public-procurement rules limit cancellation after acceptance?
Is this a standalone order, a blanket, a call-off against a blanket or contract, a consignment or VMI withdrawal, or a rush or standing order?
If this is a call-off, which blanket quantities, dates and locations does it split, and what remaining blanket balance is left?
If this is a VMI or consignment order, was it issued automatically on withdrawal, and does the seller still send an order response acknowledgement without treating it as a new offer negotiation?
Which quotation, contract or framework, catalogue and project identifiers is this order based on?
Which originator or internal requisition document caused this order to be issued?
How does this order reference WM-ECO-021 quotes and contain WM-ECO-024 fulfilment obligations without duplicating those models?
Is the order signed, with which signature profile, and what integrity hash binds the signature to the issued content?
Which additional binary or URI attachments accompany the order, and are they supporting drawings rather than a second copy of the order?
Which XSD, Schematron and profile business rules were applied, and did the instance pass the fatal Peppol and UBL constraints?
Are all fixed and calculated amounts manifested by the sender so the receiver is not required to recompute the calculation model?
Which parties, processors and auditors may read this order, and which fields are restricted to finance or legal roles?
Which contact names, employee identifiers, emails or phone numbers on the order are personal data, and what processing purpose justifies their retention?
How long must the original order data message be retained in accessible, integrity-preserving form, and when may it be deleted or anonymised without erasing the commercial cancellation history?
What exception process applies if a party needs a copy after access expiry, or if a signature was not used because Peppol Ordering does not mandate eSignature?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
